title: My Calendar II
prompt: Design a `MyCalendarTwo` class to track events, allowing double bookings but never a triple booking. A double booking is when two events have a non-empty intersection; a triple booking is when three events all share some common moment. Implement `book(start, end)`, representing an event during the half-open interval `[start, end)`. Return `True` and add the event if booking it would not create a triple booking anywhere; otherwise return `False` and do not add it.

examples.input: book(10,20)->true, book(50,60)->true, book(10,40)->true, book(5,15)->false, book(5,10)->true, book(25,55)->true
examples.explanation: book(5,15) fails because [10,15) would already be double-booked by [10,20) and [10,40), making it a triple booking.

constraints: at most 1000 calls will be made to book
hints: Track not just the booked events, but also the regions that are already double-booked, since a new event is illegal exactly when it overlaps a double-booked region.
When a new booking is accepted, any overlap it creates with existing single bookings becomes a new double-booked region — compute those overlap ranges using max(start) and min(end).

Maintain two lists: all bookings, and all currently double-booked ranges. Reject a new event if it overlaps any double-booked range; otherwise add its overlaps with existing bookings to the double-booked list, then add the event itself.

solution.approach: Keep two lists: `bookings` (every accepted event) and `overlaps` (regions currently covered by exactly two events). To book a new event, first check it against every entry in `overlaps` — if it intersects any of them, accepting it would create a triple booking, so reject. Otherwise, for every existing booking that intersects the new event, compute their overlap range [max(starts), min(ends)] and add it to `overlaps` (this correctly captures the new double-booked regions). Finally add the new event to `bookings` and accept it.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n) per booking, O(n^2) overall for n calls
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) to store bookings and overlaps
